tips.cue: Drupes fully coloured and firm; on sumacs the sticky coating has developed.
tips.collect: Strip clusters by hand. Watch that fruit persists long after ripening - old grey fruit from last season is often still attached.
tips.handling: Remove the fleshy or waxy coat. Hard seed coat usually needs scarification.
tips.caution: Confirm identity - this family includes poison oak, whose fruit is also collected by birds and looks superficially similar at a distance.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.

tips.cue: Pods leathery to papery and turning brown; seeds rattle loose inside.
tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Fruit turns from green to purple-brown and softens.
tips.collect: Pick from the tree or gather fresh drop.
tips.handling: Remove flesh immediately. Recalcitrant - do not let dry, sow fresh.

tips.cue: Capsule has gone from green to straw and the seed inside is dark, not pale.
tips.collect: Capsules dehisce explosively. Bag them, or collect the moment the first few split.
tips.handling: Dry fully in a paper bag; seed threshes itself as remaining capsules open.

tips.cue: Varies with fruit type - fleshy fruits fully coloured and slightly soft, dry achenes brown and loose.
tips.collect: Pick fleshy fruit by hand; strip plumed achenes when they detach at a touch.
tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.collect: Roll the disc gently between fingers - ripe segments break away.
tips.handling: Hard seed coat; scarify before sowing.

tips.cue: Capsule dry, brown, and beginning to split; seed black and flat.
tips.collect: Tip the capsule into a bag - ripe seed pours out.
tips.handling: Easy to clean and store. Long juvenile period - expect years to flowering.

tips.cue: Pappus (the fluff) has dried and begun to lift; heads look grey and open rather than green and tight.
tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.cue: Capsules turning from green to brown; a few on the plant have already popped.
tips.collect: Capsules explode when ripe, often within days. Bag branches or lay a sheet beneath and shake.
tips.handling: Dry in a paper bag - remaining capsules will fire and self-thresh. Most need heat and/or cold treatment to break dormancy.

tips.cue: Capsules dry and beginning to split at the tip.
tips.collect: Strip upward into a bag before the plumed seed disperses.
tips.handling: Screen out the fluff. Very small seed - use a fine sieve.
